title: The Buyback Playbook
thesis: Record share buybacks across banking, tech, and energy in the same weeks are not an earnings-season coincidence but a synchronized forecast: capital voting against its own expansion.
body:
Strip the press releases of their differences and the same move repeats across unrelated industries this quarter: record cash returned to shareholders rather than redeployed [sy_f88632f76537, sy_e4dfb9f72fad, sy_ba440e41355c]. The pattern is not a coincidence of earnings season — it is a shared read on where the economy is headed.

<instances as="cards">
<item>JPMorgan authorized a $30 billion repurchase, its largest single program on record [sy_f88632f76537].</item>
<item>Apple lifted its buyback to $110 billion, even as unit growth flattened [sy_e4dfb9f72fad].</item>
<item>ExxonMobil added $20 billion after a record quarter, choosing returns over new exploration [sy_ba440e41355c].</item>
</instances>

<quote display="hero">[qt_bd80c96400c0]</quote>

Three boards in three sectors arrived at the same conclusion in the same weeks: the safest use of a dollar right now is to hand it back [sy_f88632f76537, sy_ba440e41355c].

<callout>A buyback wave this synchronized is a forecast in disguise — capital voting, in unison, against its own expansion [sy_e4dfb9f72fad, sy_ba440e41355c]</callout>
